channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan Agree to Increase Agricultural Trade Turnover
item.description: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan have reached an agreement to boost trade in agricultural products. This deal aims to enhance economic cooperation and increase the exchange of goods between the two nations in the agricultural sector.

item.title: 25 Rescued from Apartment Building Fire in Astana
item.description: Emergency services rescued 25 people, including seven children, from a fire in a multi-story residential building in Astana. The fire, which involved household items in an apartment on the fifth floor, was successfully extinguished by the Ministry of Emergency Situations.

item.title: Germany Cannot Supply More Patriot Systems to Ukraine, Defense Minister Says
item.description: German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius stated that Berlin can no longer supply additional Patriot missile defense systems to Ukraine. He explained this decision by the weakening of Germany's own defenses and urged other partner countries to act more proactively.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Banks Sever Ties with Companies Amid Sanctions Risk Mitigation Efforts
item.description: Commercial banks in Kyrgyzstan are actively working to minimize secondary sanctions risks. 'ABank' has terminated business relations with 115 companies, and 'Eldik Bank' has severed ties with 169 organizations deemed high-risk. This coordinated effort aims to comply with international sanctions.

item.title: UN Official Warns ISIS-K Poses Serious Threat to Central, South Asia with New Technologies
item.description: Alexander Zuev, acting head of the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, warned that the Khorasan province branch of the Islamic State (ISIS-K) remains a serious terrorist threat to Central and South Asia. Speaking at the SCO Plus Security meeting in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, he stated that ISIS-K is utilizing drones and artificial intelligence for its activities, acquiring advanced tactical equipment and training. The group exploits instability through its regional branches.

item.title: Kazakhstan NOC President Golovkin Meets IOC Head Coventry in Dakar
item.description: Gennady Golovkin, President of the National Olympic Committee of Kazakhstan, met with IOC President Kirsty Coventry in Dakar. They discussed the development of the Olympic movement and preparations for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games boxing competitions. Kazakhstan has 18 athletes at the Youth Olympics, having won two medals so far.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans 202-Hectare Industrial Zone in Chuy Region
item.description: A new industrial zone spanning 202 hectares is planned for the Chuy region of Kyrgyzstan. The project aims to attract 21 enterprises with an estimated investment of 31.64 billion soms. Infrastructure development will require 600 million soms, according to President Sadyr Japarov.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Constructs 34.9 km of Irrigation Canals in Chuy Region
item.description: In the Chuy region, 34.9 kilometers of irrigation canals have been built, repaired, and cleaned as part of efforts to improve water supply. Additionally, 44.78 km of water pipelines were installed between 2021 and 2026, according to President Sadyr Japarov.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Build World's Longest Glass Suspension Bridge by 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to construct the world's longest glass suspension bridge, measuring 732 meters, in the Ala Archa National Park by the end of 2027. The project aims to be recognized in the Guinness Book of Records. This ambitious construction is expected to become a significant tourist attraction.

item.title: Kemin District in Kyrgyzstan Asphalted 72.4 km of Roads Worth 562.1 Million Som
item.description: In Kemin district, Kyrgyzstan, 72.4 km of roads have been asphalted between 2021 and 2026, with a total investment of 562.1 million som. The district's socio-economic development was reviewed by President Sadyr Japarov. The material and technical base of municipal services and agriculture is also being updated.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Orders Review of Land Dispute Involving 20 Families
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has ordered an investigation into a land dispute involving 20 families who purchased plots in 2020. The families received state acts for ownership but later faced restrictions from the State Agency for Land Resources. The president questioned why lower court rulings favoring the families were overturned.

item.title: Afghan Fruit Growers Face Economic Hardship Amidst Low Prices and Lack of Cold Storage
item.description: Fruit farmers in Afghanistan's Wardak, Kandahar, and Ghazni provinces are experiencing economic difficulties. A large supply of fruits and a shortage of cold storage facilities have led to low selling prices. Farmers report selling apples for significantly less than their value, attributing the problem to the lack of adequate storage and high costs of available facilities.

item.title: Iran executes man accused of attacking police post
item.description: Iran's judiciary has executed Mohammad-Aref Shahbakhsh from Balochistan, accused of involvement in an armed attack on a police post in Sistan and Baluchestan. State media reported he was convicted of membership in the Jaysh al-Adl group and charges of 'baghy' and 'moharebeh'. Human rights groups criticize such charges as vague and politically motivated.

item.title: Zohra Wenda Selected as New Representative for Afghan Youth at UN Civil Program
item.description: Human rights activist Zohra Wenda has been chosen as the new representative for the 'Afghan Youth at the UN' civil program for 2026-2027. Selected by the 'Afghans for Progressive Thinking' NGO after competing with three other candidates, Wenda will advocate for Afghan youth at UN sessions. This initiative provides a platform for young Afghans, particularly women, to voice their concerns internationally.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Train 100 African Specialists in Digital Technologies
item.description: Kazakhstan will provide 100 free training places for specialists from African countries in digital technologies, programming, and artificial intelligence. This initiative, part of an agreement with the ITU, aims to leverage Kazakhstan's experience in digital projects. Young Kazakhs will also gain international work experience through a Junior Professional Officers program.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Orders Review of Lab Error Case After Citizen's Plea
item.description: A Bishkek resident appealed to President Sadyr Жапаров regarding the death of his mother, alleging a misdiagnosis at the private 'Aqualab' laboratory. The citizen stated that initial tests found no cancer, but later confirmed the diagnosis, causing a critical two-month delay in treatment. The President has ordered a review of the case.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Orders Review of Housing for Visually Impaired Father of Nine
item.description: President Sadyr Жапаров has instructed the State Mortgage Company to consider providing a 98-square-meter apartment to a visually impaired father of nine. The citizen, who is on the housing queue, stated the offered apartment was too small for his family. The President emphasized considering the applicant's health and family situation for special consideration.

item.title: Tashkent Thermal Power Plant May Cease Oil Fuel Usage
item.description: The Tashkent Thermal Power Plant may stop using mazut (fuel oil). This will be achieved by energizing the 500 kV "Ring" substation, built with the participation of the World Bank, and redistributing electricity loads. The substation's commissioning is expected to facilitate this transition.

item.title: Zahra Vanda Selected as Afghanistan's Youth Representative to the UN
item.description: Zahra Vanda has been chosen as Afghanistan's sixth Youth Representative to the United Nations for the 2026-2027 term. The selection process was managed by Afghans for Progressive Thinking. Vanda will focus on gathering youth perspectives on issues like girls' education and women's rights.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Train and Employ Citizens as Cooks in Japan
item.description: Uzbekistan's Migration Agency has reached an agreement with Japanese companies and universities to train and employ 40 citizens as cooks in Japan. This initiative aims to facilitate employment opportunities for Uzbek nationals abroad through vocational training and job placement programs. Further details are expected as the program progresses.

item.title: Five Killed, Over Ten Injured in Shooting in Krakow's Historic Center
item.description: At least five people were killed and over ten injured in a shooting incident in the historic center of Krakow on Saturday, November 7. Among the wounded were two police officers. The attacker, who drove a car onto the main market square and opened fire, was apprehended by police after being wounded. The motive remains officially undisclosed.

item.title: US Forms New Task Force to Interdict Iran's Weapons Shipments
item.description: The US has established Task Force Iron Gate to disrupt weapons shipments, sanctioned materials, and military technology moving through Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. This expands existing naval blockade efforts aimed at reducing Iran's revenue and its ability to finance terrorism and rebuild military capabilities.

item.title: Qatar PM: Mediation Efforts Continue for US-Iran Agreement
item.description: Qatar's Prime Minister announced that Doha's mediation efforts between the US and Iran to reach an agreement and prevent regional escalation are ongoing. He expressed confidence in reaching a "good agreement," noting Washington's continued willingness to resolve differences despite US midterm elections. Regional countries are concerned about potential US attacks on Iran.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey Expand Investment Cooperation and Privatization Ties
item.description: Uzbekistan's Director of State Assets Management met with the Chairman of the Turkish-Uzbek Business Council to discuss attracting Turkish investors to privatization processes. A memorandum was signed to inform Turkish companies about privatization, exchange investment proposals, and establish systematic interaction. A special session for investors is planned for December.

item.title: Deputy Head of Afghanistan's National Unity Government Returns from Iran
item.description: Engineer Mohammad Khan Rahmani, deputy head of Afghanistan's National Unity Government executive office, has returned to the country from Iran, according to the Taliban's 'Commission for Contact with Afghan Personalities'. Rahmani expressed happiness upon his return and thanked the commission.

item.title: UAE Official: Risk of Military Confrontation Between US and Iran Remains
item.description: A senior UAE official expressed optimism about US-Iran nuclear negotiations but warned that the risk of military confrontation persists. He stated the UAE is planning for worst-case scenarios while hoping for the best outcome, emphasizing that diplomatic resolution is preferred. The UAE was previously targeted by Iranian missiles and drones.

item.title: Central Asian Nations Capitalize on US-China Competition for Resources
item.description: Several countries, including one in Central Asia, are benefiting from the strategic competition between the US and China for critical resources and metals. Both superpowers are investing billions in mining, allowing these nations to attract capital from both sides simultaneously. This dynamic presents significant economic opportunities.

item.title: Uzbekistan Allocates 49 Trillion Som to Healthcare, Life Expectancy Reaches 75.4 Years
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev congratulated medical workers as Uzbekistan's annual healthcare funding reached 49 trillion som. He noted the creation of medical records for over 38 million citizens via the DMED system, contributing to an increased average life expectancy of 75.4 years.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches International Initiative at UNESCO for Cultural Heritage Protection
item.description: Uzbekistan has launched an international initiative at UNESCO to enhance the protection of cultural heritage amidst globalization and climate change. Approved by the UNESCO Executive Board, the initiative aims to safeguard tangible and intangible heritage, conduct risk assessments, and strengthen international cooperation.

item.title: Over 3200 Tashkent Residents Dispute Housing Valuation Results as Overstated
item.description: More than 3,200 Tashkent property owners have reported that the results of the first mass housing valuation were overstated. Public discussions on the valuation results are extended until December 4, allowing owners to challenge or comment on the assessed values.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Garden Catering Trade Executives Sentenced to Prison for Mass Food Poisoning
item.description: In Uzbekistan's Fergana region, the head and technologist of Garden Catering Trade have been sentenced to real prison terms for the mass poisoning of 105 children in kindergartens. A cassation court revised the initial sentences of restricted freedom, imposing four years for the head and three years and six months for the technologist.

item.title: US Central Command Establishes Task Force to Disrupt Iran's Transit Routes
item.description: US Central Command (CENTCOM) has established a special task force named 'Iron Gate' to prevent Iran from using land routes for advanced weapons and other items. The task force, based in Florida, will coordinate with other US agencies to block the movement of advanced weapon systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned goods, and illicit financial flows through Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea.

item.title: Kazakhstan Extends Ban on Export of Gasoline and Diesel Fuel for Six Months
item.description: Kazakhstan has extended its ban on the export of gasoline, diesel fuel, and certain other petroleum products by road transport for another six months. The restrictions, effective from November 22, 2026, to May 22, 2027, apply to exports to Eurasian Economic Union member states as well.

item.title: Canada Rejects Afghan Teenager's Study Permit Despite Full Scholarship
item.description: Canadian immigration authorities have denied a study permit to an 18-year-old Afghan girl who had received a full scholarship to attend a British Columbia boarding school. The department cited concerns she would not return to Afghanistan and lacked sufficient funds, despite the scholarship covering all expenses.

item.title: Uzbek President Congratulates Healthcare Workers on Professional Holiday, Highlights Reforms
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev congratulated Uzbekistan's medical and pharmaceutical workers on their professional holiday, emphasizing reforms in the healthcare sector, increased funding, and improved life expectancy. He noted a sevenfold increase in healthcare financing, reaching 49 trillion soms by 2026, and the digitalization of medical services.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Provide Housing to Residents Affected by Border Conflict
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will allocate 170 houses, transferred from Tajikistan through land exchange, to residents of the Batken region. These homes are intended for citizens who lost their housing during the border conflicts in 2021-2022.

item.title: Prosecutor's Office Overturns Illegal Market Owner Requirements in Abay Region
item.description: The prosecutor's office in the Makanchy district of Abay Region has overturned an illegal requirement imposed on market owners. The district administration had mandated that market owners provide land for temporary trading objects free of charge, violating entrepreneurs' rights. The official responsible for the regulation has been fined.

item.title: West Kazakhstan Governor Classifies Rally Refusal Statistics as Confidential
item.description: The governor of West Kazakhstan region has classified statistics on refusals for peaceful rallies as confidential. The Kazakhstan International Bureau for Human Rights and Rule of Law reported this. Since May 2020, Kazakhstan has amended its laws on peaceful assemblies, requiring only prior notification instead of permits.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Security Chief Reports Rise in Extremist Online Content
item.description: Uzbekistan's State Security Service identified over 49,000 extremist and terrorist online resources in early 2026, a 14% increase from the previous year. The head of the service stated that terrorist groups increasingly use digital technologies for propaganda and operations. Uzbekistan ranks low on the Global Terrorism Index.

item.title: Astana Hosts Traditional 'Sogym-FEST' Meat Fair with Competitive Prices
item.description: Astana has launched its traditional 'Sogym-FEST' meat fair, offering products from various regions of Kazakhstan at competitive prices. Beef is sold at 3,300 tenge per kilogram, horse meat at 3,500 tenge, and lamb at 3,700 tenge. The fair aims to sell over 1,000 tons of meat by the end of the season.
